scenes.title: Farm Scene 4 — Animal Actions Around the Barn
scenes.brief: Describe familiar farm animals, what they are doing, and where they are.
targetExamples: The cow is by the barn.
The pig is in the mud.
The chickens are pecking the grain.
The sheep is near the fence.

scenes.title: Farm Scene 5 — Transport, Animals and Places
scenes.brief: Combine farm nouns, actions and simple positional language.
targetExamples: The tractor is carrying hay.
The horse is eating grass.
The goat is on the rock.
The duck is in the pond.

scenes.title: Farm Scene 6 — Garden and Growing Food
scenes.brief: Talk about garden nouns, food, locations and simple inference.
targetExamples: The carrots are growing in the garden.
The rabbit is next to the carrots.
The chicken is near the vegetables.
The scarecrow is in the garden.
The apples are on the tree.

scenes.title: Farm Scene 7 — Morning Jobs on the Farm
scenes.brief: Tell a simple farmyard story using several children doing purposeful jobs.
targetExamples: The child is watering the plants.
The child is collecting eggs.
The child is feeding the chickens.
The child is carrying the vegetables.
The child is sweeping.
First the child waters the plants, then the child feeds the chickens.

scenes.title: Farm Scene 8 — Farmyard Friends and Counting
scenes.brief: Observe familiar farm animals, compare them, and talk about number and size.
targetExamples: The cow is big.
The horse is brown.
The pig is pink.
There are three sheep.
There are two ducklings.
There are more sheep than ducklings.

scenes.title: Farm Scene 9 — Looking After the Animals
scenes.brief: Talk about what animals need and which farm job matches each need.
targetExamples: The cow needs water.
The child is carrying water to the cow.
The child is feeding the chickens.
The pig is inside the gate.
The child is picking vegetables.

scenes.brief: Farm animals with clear size, colour, texture and quantity contrasts.
targetExamples: The cow is big.
The pig is small and pink.
There are three white sheep.
There are two little yellow ducklings.
The cow is bigger than the pig.

scenes.brief: Six clear spatial examples around a farmyard: on, behind, next to, under, between and near.
targetExamples: The cat is on the hay bale.
The pig is behind the fence.
The horse is next to the barn.
The chicken is under the shelter.
The cow is between the fence posts.
The duck is near the pond.

scenes.brief: Five children each showing one purposeful farm task: watering plants, collecting eggs, feeding chickens, carrying vegetables and sweeping.
targetExamples: The child is watering the plants.
The child is collecting eggs.
The child is feeding the chickens.
The child is carrying the vegetables.
The child is sweeping.
scenes.knownVisualDeviation: The approved image contains four chickens rather than the requested three. This does not block the functional-language target because counting chickens is not a teaching objective in this scene.
